items.title: Periodic tensor grids and multilinear interpolation
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_d>0$, and let $N_1,\ldots,N_d\ge1$ be integers. The periodic rectangular box is
$$\mathbb T^d_{\ell}:=\mathbb R^d/(\ell_1\mathbb Z\times\cdots\times\ell_d\mathbb Z).$$
Set $h_j:=\ell_j/N_j$. Its uniform tensor grid has nodes $x_{\boldsymbol i}=(i_1h_1,\ldots,i_dh_d)$, indexed by $0\le i_j<N_j$, with indices understood modulo $N_j$.

For node data $V_{\boldsymbol i}$ and a lift $x\in\mathbb R^d$ of a point on the torus, define
$$q_j:=\left\lfloor x_j/h_j\right\rfloor,\qquad \theta_j:=x_j/h_j-q_j\in[0,1),$$
and for $\boldsymbol\epsilon\in\{0,1\}^d$ define
$$w_{\boldsymbol\epsilon}(x):=\prod_{j=1}^d\theta_j^{\epsilon_j}(1-\theta_j)^{1-\epsilon_j}.$$
The tensor-product multilinear interpolant is
$$\mathcal I_hV(x):=\sum_{\boldsymbol\epsilon\in\{0,1\}^d}w_{\boldsymbol\epsilon}(x)V_{([q_1+\epsilon_1]_{N_1},\ldots,[q_d+\epsilon_d]_{N_d})},$$
where $[k]_N$ is the residue in $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$. The formula is unchanged when a period $\ell_j$ is added to $x_j$, so it defines an interpolant on $\mathbb T^d_{\ell}$. If $N_j=1$, the two corner indices in that coordinate coincide; the formula still gives the same node value.

For a continuous periodic function $v$, $\mathcal I_hv$ means the interpolant of its grid samples. Put $h:=\max_jh_j$.

references.title: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, Numerical Methods, Meteorological Training Course Lecture Series, 2002
Lukas Einkemmer and Alexander Ostermann, On the error propagation of semi-Lagrange and Fourier methods for advection problems, Computers & Mathematics with Applications 69 (2015), 170–179

items.title: A periodic C1 velocity has a global characteristic flow on a finite horizon
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $T>0$, $\ell_j>0$, and let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $[0,T]$. Suppose $b:J\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ is $C^1$ and periodic in $x_j$ with period $\ell_j$ for every $j$. Choose a compact interval $K\subset J$ with $[0,T]\subset\operatorname{int}K$, and put $M_K:=\sup_{K\times[0,\ell_1]\times\cdots\times[0,\ell_d]}\|b\|_2$. For every $s\in[0,T]$ and $x\in\mathbb R^d$, there is a unique solution $X(\cdot;s,x)$ of
$$X'(t)=b(t,X(t)),\qquad X(s;s,x)=x,$$
on the whole interval $[0,T]$. The lifted flow is periodic-equivariant:
$$X(t;s,x+\boldsymbol k\boldsymbol\ell)=X(t;s,x)+\boldsymbol k\boldsymbol\ell\qquad(\boldsymbol k\in\mathbb Z^d),$$
where $\boldsymbol k\boldsymbol\ell=(k_1\ell_1,\ldots,k_d\ell_d)$. If $M_T:=\sup_{[0,T]\times[0,\ell_1]\times\cdots\times[0,\ell_d]}\|b\|_2$, then
$$\|X(t;s,x)-x\|_2\le M_T|t-s|\qquad(t\in[0,T]).$$
Thus each characteristic stays in a compact tube $[0,T]\times\overline B(x,M_TT+1)$.

references.title: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, Numerical Methods, Meteorological Training Course Lecture Series, 2002
Lukas Einkemmer and Alexander Ostermann, On the error propagation of semi-Lagrange and Fourier methods for advection problems, Computers & Mathematics with Applications 69 (2015), 170–179

items.title: A transverse backward boundary hit has a certified time and trace error bound
items.statement:
Let $J=[a,b]$ be a compact bracket, let $y$ be an exact incoming characteristic on $J$, and let $g(t,x)$ be a boundary guard that is $L_g$-Lipschitz in its state argument on a tube containing the exact path and a dense reconstruction $U$. Suppose $h(t):=g(t,y(t))$ has a root $\tau\in J$ and a declared orientation $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}$ with $\sigma h'(t)\ge\nu>0$ throughout $J$. If
$$\sup_{t\in J}\|y(t)-U(t)\|_2\le\eta,\qquad |g(\widehat\tau,U(\widehat\tau))|\le\varepsilon,\qquad \widehat\tau\in J,$$
then the matched first-hit time satisfies
$$|\widehat\tau-\tau|\le\Delta:=\frac{L_g\eta+\varepsilon}{\nu}.$$
If the boundary value $\beta(t,x)$ is Lipschitz in time and state with constants $L_t^\beta,L_x^\beta$ on the same tube and $\|y'(t)\|_2\le M$, then
$$|\beta(\widehat\tau,U(\widehat\tau))-\beta(\tau,y(\tau))|\le L_t^\beta\Delta+L_x^\beta(\eta+M\Delta).$$
This is a local one-hit bound. It gives no conclusion at grazing, unresolved, or simultaneous events.

references.title: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, Numerical Methods, Meteorological Training Course Lecture Series, 2002
Lukas Einkemmer and Alexander Ostermann, On the error propagation of semi-Lagrange and Fourier methods for advection problems, Computers & Mathematics with Applications 69 (2015), 170–179

items.title: Explicit Euler characteristic backtracking with multilinear interpolation
items.statement:
Inputs are a periodic grid from [[def-semilagrangian-periodic-grid-and-interpolant]], a finite horizon $T>0$, a positive integer $M$ of time steps, a periodic $C^1$ velocity $b$, periodic initial data $u_0$, node values $U^0_{\boldsymbol i}=u_0(x_{\boldsymbol i})$, and a nonnegative integer step budget $B$. Write $\Delta t=T/M$ and $t_n=n\Delta t$. The output is either `success` with $U^0,\ldots,U^M$, or `budget-exhausted` with no partial final state.

1. If $B<M$, return `budget-exhausted` before changing the input data.
2. For $n=0,\ldots,M-1$ and each arrival node $x_{\boldsymbol i}$, compute the explicit backward Euler foot lift
   $$\widetilde x_{\boldsymbol i}^{\,n}:=x_{\boldsymbol i}-\Delta t\,b(t_{n+1},x_{\boldsymbol i}).$$
   Reduce each coordinate modulo its period when evaluating the periodic interpolant.
3. Set
   $$U_{\boldsymbol i}^{n+1}:=\mathcal I_h U^n(\widetilde x_{\boldsymbol i}^{\,n}).$$
4. After the $M$ finite updates, return `success` with all node arrays.

The finite step budget counts time updates. Every update evaluates one foot per grid node and a finite sum of $2^d$ interpolation terms. The procedure imposes no bound on $\|b\|\Delta t/h$; the floor-and-fraction convention in the interpolation definition applies even when a foot crosses many grid cells.

references.title: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, Numerical Methods, Meteorological Training Course Lecture Series, 2002
Lukas Einkemmer and Alexander Ostermann, On the error propagation of semi-Lagrange and Fourier methods for advection problems, Computers & Mathematics with Applications 69 (2015), 170–179

items.title: Periodic multilinear interpolation is convex and L-infinity contractive
items.statement:
For the periodic tensor interpolant of [[def-semilagrangian-periodic-grid-and-interpolant]], every value is a convex combination of the $2^d$ corner data. Consequently nonnegative data remain nonnegative, the interpolant lies between the minimum and maximum corner values, and for any node arrays $V,W$,
$$\|\mathcal I_hV-\mathcal I_hW\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb T^d_\ell)}\le\|V-W\|_{\ell^\infty}.$$
These conclusions hold at every foot, with no displacement-to-cell-size restriction.

references.title: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, Numerical Methods, Meteorological Training Course Lecture Series, 2002
Lukas Einkemmer and Alexander Ostermann, On the error propagation of semi-Lagrange and Fourier methods for advection problems, Computers & Mathematics with Applications 69 (2015), 170–179

items.title: A periodic C1 characteristic map is an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism
items.statement:
Under the hypotheses of [[thm-periodic-c1-velocity-has-global-characteristic-flow]], fix $s,t\in[0,T]$ and let $\Phi_{t,s}(x):=X(t;s,x)$ on the periodic lift $\mathbb R^d$. Then $\Phi_{t,s}$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism with inverse $\Phi_{s,t}$, and
$$\det D_x\Phi_{t,s}(x)>0\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^d).$$

references.title: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, Numerical Methods, Meteorological Training Course Lecture Series, 2002
Lukas Einkemmer and Alexander Ostermann, On the error propagation of semi-Lagrange and Fourier methods for advection problems, Computers & Mathematics with Applications 69 (2015), 170–179

items.title: Tensor multilinear interpolation has a second-derivative error bound
items.statement:
Let $u\in C^2(\mathbb T^d_\ell)$ and let $h_j$ be the coordinate mesh widths in [[def-semilagrangian-periodic-grid-and-interpolant]]. Then
$$\|\mathcal I_hu-u\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb T^d_\ell)}\le\frac18\sum_{j=1}^dh_j^2\|\partial_{jj}u\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb T^d_\ell)}.$$
The estimate includes grid nodes and periodic cell endpoints.

references.title: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, Numerical Methods, Meteorological Training Course Lecture Series, 2002
Lukas Einkemmer and Alexander Ostermann, On the error propagation of semi-Lagrange and Fourier methods for advection problems, Computers & Mathematics with Applications 69 (2015), 170–179

items.title: Explicit Euler gives a second-order local backward-foot defect
items.statement:
Let $b\in C^1([0,T]\times\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)$ be periodic in space, and set
$$M:=\sup\|b\|_2,\qquad L_x:=\sup\|D_xb\|,\qquad L_t:=\sup\|\partial_tb\|_2,$$
where the suprema are over one full periodic time-space cylinder. For $0\le t_n<t_{n+1}\le T$, $\Delta t=t_{n+1}-t_n$, and an arrival lift $x$, let $X(t_n;t_{n+1},x)$ be the exact backward characteristic foot. The explicit Euler foot $x-\Delta t\,b(t_{n+1},x)$ satisfies
$$\bigl\|X(t_n;t_{n+1},x)-(x-\Delta t\,b(t_{n+1},x))\bigr\|_2\le\frac12(L_xM+L_t)(\Delta t)^2.$$
The estimate is local for every positive $\Delta t$; it requires no relation between displacement and grid width.

references.title: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, Numerical Methods, Meteorological Training Course Lecture Series, 2002
Lukas Einkemmer and Alexander Ostermann, On the error propagation of semi-Lagrange and Fourier methods for advection problems, Computers & Mathematics with Applications 69 (2015), 170–179

items.title: Characteristic departure cells are measurable and have positive finite volume
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^d(0,\ell_j)$ be the bounded open fundamental box used for Lebesgue measure, and let $Q=\prod_{j=1}^d[0,\ell_j)$ be its half-open grid-indexing copy. Let $\Phi$ be the periodic $C^1$ characteristic diffeomorphism of [[lem-periodic-characteristic-map-is-orientation-preserving]], and let $A_i\subseteq Q$ be a Lebesgue-measurable arrival cell with $|A_i|:=\lambda_d(A_i\cap\Omega)>0$. Then $D_i:=\Phi^{-1}(A_i)$, interpreted on the torus and represented in $\Omega$, is Lebesgue measurable and satisfies
$$0<|D_i|<\infty.$$
This includes every finite tensor-grid cell with nonempty interior. The departure cells form a partition up to null sets whenever a finite family of arrival cells does; an exact torus partition pulls back to an exact torus partition.

references.title: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, Numerical Methods, Meteorological Training Course Lecture Series, 2002
Lukas Einkemmer and Alexander Ostermann, On the error propagation of semi-Lagrange and Fourier methods for advection problems, Computers & Mathematics with Applications 69 (2015), 170–179

items.title: Characteristic-cell overlap remapping for a conservative density
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for this Lebesgue-measurable-volume branch. Work on the periodic box $\mathbb T^d_\ell$ of [[def-semilagrangian-periodic-grid-and-interpolant]]. For measure calculations use the bounded open fundamental domain $\Omega:=\prod_{j=1}^d(0,\ell_j)$; the period faces omitted from the half-open grid-indexing copy $Q=\prod_{j=1}^d[0,\ell_j)$ are Lebesgue-null by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]]. For a periodic measurable set $E$, define $|E|:=\lambda_d(E\cap\Omega)$, where $\lambda_d$ is the $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measure of [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]. Let $\{C_j\}_{j=1}^J$ be a finite measurable source-cell partition and $\{A_i\}_{i=1}^J$ a finite measurable arrival-cell partition of $\Omega$ up to null sets, with every cell of positive volume; their grid labels use the half-open convention in $Q$. Let $\Phi=\Phi_{t_{n+1},t_n}$ be the exact characteristic map from time $t_n$ to $t_{n+1}$. Its inverse images $D_i:=\Phi^{-1}(A_i)$ are the **departure cells**; [[lem-periodic-flow-departure-cells-have-positive-finite-volume]] gives their measurability and positive finite volume, while [[lem-periodic-characteristic-map-is-orientation-preserving]] gives the diffeomorphism and positive-Jacobian convention.

Given a source cell-average density $\rho_j^n$ on $C_j$, set
$$\overline\rho_i:=\frac{1}{|D_i|}\sum_{j=1}^J|D_i\cap C_j|\rho_j^n,\qquad \rho_i^{n+1}:=\frac{|D_i|}{|A_i|}\overline\rho_i.$$
The first formula is the exact intersection-volume remap of [[def-intersection-volume-conservative-remapping]] from the source partition to the departure partition. The second is the characteristic volume factor that converts the average on a departure cell into the transported mass per arrival-cell volume. All intersections and volumes are exact in this mathematical definition; a geometric approximation or quadrature rule would require a separate error term.

references.title: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, Numerical Methods, Meteorological Training Course Lecture Series, 2002
Lukas Einkemmer and Alexander Ostermann, On the error propagation of semi-Lagrange and Fourier methods for advection problems, Computers & Mathematics with Applications 69 (2015), 170–179

items.title: Periodic semi-Lagrangian error is controlled by local foot and interpolation defects
items.statement:
Fix $T>0$ and a periodic box with grid width $h=\max_j h_j$. Let $u\in C^1([0,T];C^2(\mathbb T^d_\ell))$ solve the nonconservative linear transport equation
$$u_t+b\cdot\nabla u=0,$$
with the periodic $C^1$ velocity and global flow of [[thm-periodic-c1-velocity-has-global-characteristic-flow]]. Consider $N$ equal time steps $\Delta t=T/N$ and node updates
$U_{\boldsymbol i}^{n+1}=(\mathcal J_h U^n)(\widetilde x_{\boldsymbol i}^{\,n}),$
where $\mathcal J_h$ reconstructs a nodal array as a periodic function and $\widetilde x_{\boldsymbol i}^{\,n}$ is a computed backward foot. Suppose constants $\Lambda\ge1$, $C_I\ge0$, and $C_F\ge0$ are uniform over the refinement family and independent of $h,\Delta t,N$. Assume $\|\mathcal J_hV-\mathcal J_hW\|_{L^\infty}\le\Lambda\|V-W\|_{\ell^\infty}$ for all node arrays, the pointwise interpolation defect at each computed foot is at most $C_Ih^{r+1}$ for the exact samples $u^n_{\boldsymbol i}=u(x_{\boldsymbol i},t_n)$, and, for compatible lifts of the computed and exact feet, the foot error satisfies
$\|\widetilde x_{\boldsymbol i}^{\,n}-X(t_n;t_{n+1},x_{\boldsymbol i})\|_2\le C_F(\Delta t)^{q+1}$,
for integers $q,r\ge1$. If $L_u:=\sup_{[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d_\ell}\|\nabla u\|_2$ and $E_n:=\max_{\boldsymbol i}|U_{\boldsymbol i}^n-u(x_{\boldsymbol i},t_n)|$, then, with
$$\delta_h:=C_Ih^{r+1}+\Lambda L_u C_F(\Delta t)^{q+1},$$
$$E_N\le\Lambda^NE_0+\delta_h\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\Lambda^k.$$
In the contractive case $\Lambda=1$, this becomes
$$E_N\le E_0+T\left(C_I\frac{h^{r+1}}{\Delta t}+L_uC_F(\Delta t)^q\right).$$
For the explicit Euler and tensor multilinear algorithm, [[lem-euler-backward-characteristic-foot-error]], [[lem-periodic-tensor-interpolation-hessian-error]], and [[lem-periodic-tensor-interpolant-is-convex-and-linf-contracting]] give $q=r=1$ and $\Lambda=1$. Thus convergence for this branch follows, for example, when $E_0\to0$, $\Delta t\to0$, and $h^2/\Delta t\to0$. No classical advective CFL restriction is used; the joint consistency refinement is still required by this bound.

references.title: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, Numerical Methods, Meteorological Training Course Lecture Series, 2002
Lukas Einkemmer and Alexander Ostermann, On the error propagation of semi-Lagrange and Fourier methods for advection problems, Computers & Mathematics with Applications 69 (2015), 170–179

items.title: Characteristic-cell overlap remapping preserves mass and positivity
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the finite measurable positive-volume partition hypotheses in [[def-characteristic-cell-overlap-remapping]]. For nonnegative source averages $\rho_j^n\ge0$, the characteristic-cell overlap remap satisfies $\rho_i^{n+1}\ge0$ for every arrival cell and
$$\sum_i|D_i|\overline\rho_i=\sum_j|C_j|\rho_j^n.$$
In particular, it satisfies
$$\sum_i|A_i|\rho_i^{n+1}=\sum_j|C_j|\rho_j^n.$$
The proof applies [[thm-overlap-remap-l2-projection-conservation-positivity]] to the source partition $\{C_j\}$ and departure partition $\{D_i\}$; its stated Countable Choice assumption is included here.

references.title: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, Numerical Methods, Meteorological Training Course Lecture Series, 2002
Lukas Einkemmer and Alexander Ostermann, On the error propagation of semi-Lagrange and Fourier methods for advection problems, Computers & Mathematics with Applications 69 (2015), 170–179

items.title: A constant-speed foot can cross many cells in one stable update
items.statement: Take the one-dimensional torus of length $1$, $16$ uniform cells of width $h=1/16$, constant velocity $b=1$, one step $\Delta t=3/10$, and arrival node $x_0=0$. The Courant displacement is $b\Delta t/h=4.8$, so the backtracked foot crosses more than four cells. Give the two grid nodes bracketing that foot values $2$ and $10$.

references.title: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, Numerical Methods, Meteorological Training Course Lecture Series, 2002

items.title: Refining time alone leaves interpolation diffusion on a fixed grid
items.statement:
Fix an integer $N\ge4$, the unit torus, and $h=1/N$. Let $b=1$ and use final time $T=h$, but split it into $K$ steps of length $\Delta t=h/K$. The smooth periodic initial function
$$u_0(x):=\prod_{j=1}^{N-1}\frac{\sin^2(\pi(x-j/N))}{\sin^2(-\pi j/N)}$$
has grid samples $U_0^0=1$ and $U_j^0=0$ for $1\le j<N$. Exact transport over $T=h$ shifts those samples by exactly one node. The semi-Lagrangian method, however, performs $K$ fractional linear interpolations on the same fixed spatial grid.

references.title: Lukas Einkemmer and Alexander Ostermann, On the error propagation of semi-Lagrange and Fourier methods for advection problems, Computers & Mathematics with Applications 69 (2015), 170–179

items.title: Variable-foot pointwise interpolation can change the grid sum
items.statement:
Use the period-$3$ one-dimensional grid with nodes $0,1,2$, $h=1$, and one time step $\Delta t=1$. Set
$$b(x)=\frac5{12}-\frac16\cos\!\left(\frac{2\pi x}{3}\right)-\frac1{2\sqrt3}\sin\!\left(\frac{2\pi x}{3}\right).$$
This is a smooth periodic velocity. Start with grid values $(U_0,U_1,U_2)=(0,0,1)$, which are samples of the smooth nonnegative period-$3$ function
$$u_0(x)=\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\pi x}{3}\right)\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\pi(x-1)}{3}\right).$$

references.title: Lukas Einkemmer and Alexander Ostermann, On the error propagation of semi-Lagrange and Fourier methods for advection problems, Computers & Mathematics with Applications 69 (2015), 170–179

items.title: A smooth deforming flow remaps two cell averages conservatively
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. On the unit torus take the smooth autonomous velocity $b(x)=\sin(2\pi x)$ and any fixed time $T>0$. Its exact flow $\Phi=\Phi_{T,0}$ is an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism. Use source and arrival cells $C_1=A_1=[0,1/4)$ and $C_2=A_2=[1/4,1)$ in a fundamental interval, with initial cell averages $(\rho_1^0,\rho_2^0)=(1,0)$. The flow fixes $0$ and $1/2$; on $(0,1/2)$ it moves points strictly to the right. Define $r:=\Phi^{-1}(1/4)$.

references.title: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, Numerical Methods, Meteorological Training Course Lecture Series, 2002
